themes.title: AI Capex Supercycle
themes.status_note: Continuing: QQQ +0.9% Monday to $756.20; Nasdaq Composite record 27,477 on Nvidia/Microsoft leadership into earnings season.
themes.body_text:
The AI capex chain opened the new week with confirmation: QQQ gained 0.9% Monday to close at $756.20 while the
Nasdaq Composite set its first record since Sep 22 at 27,477 (+1.05%), led by Nvidia and Microsoft as oil's
pullback cleared the tape for earnings season. The setup is unchanged from Friday — hyperscalers funding
roughly $200B of 2026 data-center build with debt (Barclays), NDX forward multiples digested to 21.7x (down
14% from the high), and October hike odds below 25% after the +29k payrolls shock. Breadth is the honest
caveat: the S&P added only 0.66% and sits 0.3% below its August record while the Nasdaq sprints, so this is a
mega-cap-tech move, not a market-wide one. So what: the "verify the revenue" phase continues — own links with
orders and backlog, not multiple-expansion stories. What next: the earnings runway starts with hyperscaler Q3
capex guidance from late October (master switch for the chain) and NVDA's own print on Nov 25; any guidance
cut reprices the whole chain at once.
themes.explainer:
Hyperscaler = cloud vendors building their own hyperscale data centers. NDX 21.7x is forward P/E
(Citadel Securities). Returns are Price Return on unadjusted closes (Yahoo Finance): 1W vs Sep 28 close,
1M vs Sep 4 adjusted close, YTD vs Dec 30, 2025 adjusted close. QQQ tracks the Nasdaq-100 excluding
dividends.

themes.title: Canadian Bank Earnings Momentum
themes.status_note: Still Fading: ZEB -0.5% Monday to C$73.04 against a flat TSX; December Q4 results and the Oct 28 BoC decision are the next checkpoints.
themes.body_text:
Monday added another small exhibit to the downgrade file: ZEB slipped 0.5% to C$73.04 while the TSX finished
essentially flat at 35,518.55 — banks underperforming the home market for a second straight week as the
"richest valuations since 2010" overhang meets institutional trimming that began in September. Nothing in the
Q3 fundamentals changed — record Big Six prints (RBC $6B net income, TD's $13B+ return pipeline) stand — but
the mix problem is now consensus: fee and trading income carried the beats while personal-banking credit
stayed soft, and RBC's Q3 provisions (+14%) are the line to watch into Q4. With USD/CAD at 1.4250 near a
52-week high, cross-border and tariff headlines add one more overhang for December. So what: the call stays
"hold and watch," not "buy the dip" — the excess-return phase (+15.7pp YTD) is history until Q4 proves the
credit cycle clean. What next: the Oct 28 BoC decision (NIM and mortgage-renewal read) comes first, then
early-December Q4 results must show personal-banking revival with provisions stable; further provision builds
plus fading capital-markets income would push this file from Fading to Dead.
themes.explainer:
CET1 (common equity tier 1 ratio): the higher it is, the more excess capital is available for buybacks and
dividends. TD targets 13% by 2027; at 14.3% today that implies $13B+ of potential returns. Returns are Price
Return on unadjusted closes (Yahoo Finance): 1W vs Sep 28 close, 1M vs Sep 4 adjusted close, YTD vs Dec 30,
2025 adjusted close. ZEB is the equal-weight Big Six ETF; with bank dividend yields around 2.8-3%, Total
Return would read higher.

themes.title: Middle East Supply Shock: The Oil War Premium
themes.status_note: Continuing: OPEC+ held November quotas steady; crude fell ~2% on reserve releases but XLE still gained 1% — the premium is compressing, not collapsing.
themes.body_text:
Sunday's OPEC+ verdict landed exactly as the cautious expected: the seven core producers (Saudi Arabia, Russia,
Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, Oman) held November quotas unchanged, with the next review on Nov 1 and a
full ministerial on Nov 29. With the Iran war still shutting in large volumes, most of 2026's paper output
increases never reached the market — the group concedes meaningful changes are unlikely before 2027. Monday's
market read the decision as neutral-to-soft: Brent fell 1.9% to $100.32 and WTI settled near $89.30 (-2.0%) as
G7 reserve-release signals and steady quotas combined, while energy equities diverged upward — XLE gained 1.0%
to $63.45, extending its YTD run to +43.9% (+31.2pp over SPX). So what: the premium is compressing on diplomacy
and barrels, not collapsing on fundamentals — physical tightness (sub-five-year-average stocks, deep
backwardation) still underwrites $90+ WTI. Keep exposure in upstream-heavy equities, not futures. What next:
Wednesday's EIA stocks print tests the physical case; Nov 1 decides December quotas; any US-Iran framework
headline remains the fastest way to lose the premium.
themes.explainer:
Backwardation = front-month contracts priced above deferred months, signaling physical tightness. War premium =
the geopolitics-driven slice of the price; history shows it unwinds fast once supply recovers. Returns are
Price Return on unadjusted closes (Yahoo Finance): 1W vs Sep 28 close, 1M vs Sep 4 adjusted close, YTD vs
Dec 30, 2025 adjusted close. XLE is the US energy-sector ETF (about 91% oil & gas companies), not a crude
tracker.

themes.title: Long-End Repricing: 10Y Above 5%
themes.status_note: Upgraded to Continuing: the 10Y closed Monday at a new 5.31% high even as the Nasdaq set a record — weak data cannot rally bonds, and strong data cannot either.
themes.body_text:
The long end keeps writing its own script. Monday's tape was the cleanest test yet: the Nasdaq closed at a
record 27,477 (+1.05%) and the S&P added 0.66% to 7,774 — yet the 10Y still pushed to a new closing high of
5.31%, up from 5.28% Friday. Friday had already delivered the mirror image: payrolls of just +29k (vs +85k
expected) crushed October hike odds below 25%, and the 10Y still finished at 5.28%. Neither weak growth nor
strong risk appetite can pull yields down; the driver is term premium and supply, not policy expectations.
So what: the trade expression stays short duration — TLT fell another 0.5% Monday to $77.11 and is now -9.2%
YTD, lagging SPX by nearly 22 points. The stock-bond seesaw is broken in both directions, which keeps discount
rates elevated across all risk assets even on record-equity days. What next: September CPI on Oct 14 is the
last clean inflation read before the Oct 27-28 FOMC; a soft core print that still fails to dent 5%+ yields
would cement the term-premium regime, while any dovish surprise plus a break back below 5% puts this theme on
watch.
themes.explainer:
Term premium = the extra compensation investors demand for holding long bonds, unrelated to policy
expectations; typically driven by supply (issuance), inflation uncertainty, and foreign demand. Returns are
Price Return on unadjusted closes (Yahoo Finance): 1W vs Sep 28 close, 1M vs Sep 4 adjusted close, YTD vs
Dec 30, 2025 adjusted close. The way to trade this theme is short TLT or shortening portfolio duration —
the table shows TLT itself.

performance.benchmark_rationale: A rates theme has no direct index benchmark; SPX is shown to frame the stock-bond seesaw in relative terms. Trade direction is short duration.
